plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. With a value of $3, bidding exactly $3 ensures I only win when profitable (paying less than $3) and maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only that competing bid, ensuring non-negative profit. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks losses. With no repeated interaction across values (single round), truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' behavior. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above value risks negative profit, and bidding below value only reduces chances of winning profitable auctions. With a value of $11, I should bid exactly $11 to maximize expected profit.
